cues.text: A 58-year-old man, a smoker, has severe cramp-like pains in his right upper limb.
They are particularly strong when the arm is hyperabducted.
He also suffers from attacks of fainting,
and he has disturbances of his vision as well.
Imaging shows a pulsatile swelling compressing his subclavian artery.
Now blood flows backwards in the vertebral artery: retrograde flow.
That blood is redirected to supply the arm.
This is subclavian steal. It robs the vertebrobasilar circulation, causing his fainting and visual symptoms.
